newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Levy to visit Jordan despite water row.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Levy to visit Jordan despite water row.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said on Wednesday an invitation he received to visit Jordan showed the two countries relations were not in crisis despite a row over water.

Jordan cancelled a meeting on Tuesday between Crown Prince Hassan and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu because of disagreements over water supplies promised to the Arab kingdom under a 1994 peace treaty.
"I think that the matter of yesterday was exaggerated beyond proportion," Levy told Israel Army radio.
King Hussein telephoned Netanyahu on Tuesday evening to try to work out difference over the water issue, a senior Israeli official who did not want to be identified said.
"I have received an invitation to visit Jordan and the date will be coordinated within the coming days," Levy said. He did not say from whom he had received the invitation.
Hassan and Netanyahu were to have held talks during a ceremony for seven Israeli girls killed by a Jordanian soldier near their joint border in March.

Israel cancelled the whole memorial ceremony in the wake of Prince Hassan's decision to stay away. The row cast a shadow over relations between Israel and Jordan, which has forged close ties with the Jewish state in the last three years.

Jordan officials said on Tuesday Israel backed out at the last minute from an accord to fulfil its peace treaty pledge to help the kingdom, facing growing water shortages, find an extra 50 million cubic metres of water a year.
The peace treaty, ending a 46-year state of war, specified that within a year of its coming into force in November 1994 the two sides would develop a plan to supply Jordan with the water.
Ideas for the water supply included desalination plants, dam building, and steps to ease pollution of river waters.
But no such plan was formally implemented.

Jordanian Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawneh spoke earlier this week of a "frustration in the whole peace process" and said Israel's failure to follow up its commitment to help find water supplies for Jordan was a breach of the 1994 treaty.
The ceremony in memory of the March 13 killing was to have been held at a Jordanian beauty spot leased to Israeli farmers and known in Israel as the Island of Peace.
